Chemistry.text: Which of the following curve represents the first order reaction ?
Chemistry.solution: For a first order reaction, half-life $t_{1/2} = \frac{0.693}{k}$, which is independent of the initial concentration $[R]_0$. Therefore, the plot of $t_{1/2}$ vs $[R]_0$ is a horizontal straight line parallel to the concentration axis.

Chemistry.text: Which of the following solutions will have the lowest freezing point in water ?
Chemistry.solution: Freezing point depression is a colligative property: $\Delta T_f = i \cdot K_f \cdot m$. $\text{CaCl}_2$ dissociates into 3 ions ($i = 3$), providing the maximum number of particles and highest depression in freezing point, resulting in the lowest freezing point.
Chemistry.topic: Depression of Freezing Point and van't Hoff Factor

Chemistry.text: Which of the following is not a transition metal ?
Chemistry.solution: Mercury (Hg) has completely filled d-orbitals ($3d^{10}$) in its elemental state as well as in its common oxidation states, so it is not regarded as a transition metal.

Chemistry.text: Which of the following represents the fraction of molecules with energies equal to or greater than $E_a$ ?
Chemistry.solution: According to Boltzmann distribution/Arrhenius equation, the fraction of molecules with kinetic energy equal to or greater than activation energy $E_a$ is given by $x = e^{-E_a/RT}$.
Chemistry.topic: Temperature Dependence of the Rate of a Reaction

Chemistry.text: What will happen during the electrolysis of aqueous solution of $\text{CuCl}_2$ by using platinum electrodes ?
options: (B) $\text{H}_2$ gas will be released at cathode
(C) $\text{O}_2$ gas will be released at anode
(D) $\text{Cl}_2$ gas will be released at anode
Chemistry.solution: During electrolysis of aqueous $\text{CuCl}_2$, copper ion $\text{Cu}^{2+}$ is reduced at cathode to form $\text{Cu}(s)$, while chloride ion $\text{Cl}^-$ is oxidized at anode to release $\text{Cl}_2$ gas due to overpotential of oxygen.

Chemistry.text: Aspirin is obtained by acetylation of
Chemistry.solution: Aspirin (acetylsalicylic acid) is produced by the acetylation of 2-hydroxybenzoic acid (salicylic acid) using acetic anhydride in the presence of an acid catalyst.

Chemistry.text: The secondary valency of Co in the complex $[\text{Co}(\text{NH}_3)_5(\text{NO}_2)]^{2+}$ is
Chemistry.solution: Secondary valency corresponds to the coordination number of the central metal atom/ion. Here, Co is attached to 5 $\text{NH}_3$ ligands and 1 $\text{NO}_2^-$ ligand, making total coordination number = 6.

Chemistry.text: At low temperature, phenol reacts with dil. $\text{HNO}_3$ to yield
Chemistry.solution: Phenol reacts with dilute nitric acid at low temperature (298 K) to give a mixture of ortho-nitrophenol and para-nitrophenol.

Chemistry.text: Which of the following is 'not' true about enantiomers ?
options: (A) They have the same chemical reactivity.
(B) They have the same specific rotation.
(C) They have the same melting or boiling point.
(D) They have the same refractive index.
Chemistry.solution: Enantiomers have equal magnitude of specific rotation, but opposite signs (+ and -). Thus, saying they have the exact same specific rotation is not true.

Chemistry.text: Aniline on direct nitration yields
Chemistry.solution: Direct nitration of aniline yields 51% para, 47% meta, and 2% ortho derivatives because in strongly acidic medium, aniline gets protonated to form anilinium ion which is meta-directing.

Chemistry.text: Which of the following amines has lowest $\text{pK}_b$ value ?
Chemistry.solution: Lowest $\text{pK}_b$ corresponds to the strongest base. $\text{C}_6\text{H}_5-\text{NH}(\text{CH}_3)$ (N-methylaniline) has lower $\text{pK}_b$ than aniline and p-nitroaniline due to electron-donating +I effect of the methyl group on Nitrogen atom.

Chemistry.text: The deficiency of which of the following vitamins causes increased fragility of red blood cells and muscular weakness :
Chemistry.solution: Deficiency of Vitamin E causes increased fragility of RBCs and muscular weakness.

Chemistry.text:
Assertion (A) : It is not possible to separate the components of an azeotrope by fractional distillation.
Reason (R) : Components of an azeotrope have the same composition in liquid and vapour phase and boil at a constant temperature.
options: (A) Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).
(B) Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).
(C) Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
(D) Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.
Chemistry.solution: Azeotropes boil at a constant temperature and have identical liquid and vapour compositions, so they cannot be separated by fractional distillation.

Chemistry.text:
Assertion (A) : The presence of $-\text{OH}$ group in phenols directs the incoming group to meta position in the ring.
Reason (R) : $-\text{OH}$ group in phenols activates the aromatic ring towards electrophilic substitution reaction.
options: (A) Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).
(B) Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).
(C) Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
(D) Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.
Chemistry.solution: Assertion is false because $-\text{OH}$ group is ortho- and para-directing. Reason is true as $-\text{OH}$ activates the benzene ring via resonance (+R effect).

Chemistry.text:
Assertion (A) : Actinoids show wide range of oxidation states.
Reason (R) : Actinoids are radioactive in nature.
options: (A) Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).
(B) Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).
(C) Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
(D) Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.
Chemistry.solution: Actinoids exhibit a wider range of oxidation states due to comparable energies of 5f, 6d and 7s orbitals. Though actinoids are radioactive, radioactivity is not the cause for their variable oxidation states.

Chemistry.text:
Assertion (A) : The pentaacetate of glucose does not react with $\text{H}_2\text{N}-\text{OH}$.
Reason (R) : It indicates the presence of free $-\text{CHO}$ group in glucose.
options: (A) Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).
(B) Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).
(C) Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
(D) Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.
Chemistry.solution: Assertion is true because glucose pentaacetate does not react with hydroxylamine. Reason is false because this behavior indicates the absence of a free $-\text{CHO}$ group (it exists as cyclic hemiacetal structure).

Chemistry.text:
What type of deviation from Raoult's law is shown by a mixture of phenol and aniline ? Give reason.
What will happen to the boiling point of the solution on mixing phenol and aniline ?
Chemistry.correct:
1. Negative deviation from Raoult's law.
2. Reason: Intermolecular hydrogen bonding between phenolic proton and lone pair on nitrogen of aniline is stronger than solute-solute and solvent-solvent interactions.
3. The boiling point of the solution will increase (forms maximum boiling azeotrope).
Chemistry.solution:
1. Phenol and aniline form a mixture that shows negative deviation from Raoult's law.
2. Reason: Stronger intermolecular hydrogen bonding is formed between the phenolic hydroxyl proton and the nitrogen atom of aniline compared to individual phenol-phenol and aniline-aniline interactions.
3. The boiling point increases as vapor pressure decreases below ideal value.

Chemistry.text: Why are haloarenes less reactive towards nucleophilic substitution reaction ? Give two reasons.
Chemistry.correct:
1. Resonance effect: C-X bond develops partial double bond character.
2. Difference in hybridization: Carbon attached to halogen is $sp^2$ hybridized, holding electrons more tightly.
Chemistry.solution:
Reasons for low reactivity of haloarenes:
1. Resonance effect: Lone pair on halogen delocalizes with pi electrons of aromatic ring, giving partial double bond character to C-X bond.
2. Hybridization: $sp^2$ hybridized carbon of C-X bond has greater s-character and electronegativity than $sp^3$ carbon in haloalkanes.

Chemistry.text:
(a) Write IUPAC names of the following coordination compounds :
(i) $[\text{Ag}(\text{NH}_3)_2][\text{Ag}(\text{CN})_2]$
(ii) $\text{K}_3[\text{Fe}(\text{C}_2\text{O}_4)_3]$

OR

(b) (i) Give a chemical test to show that $[\text{Co}(\text{NH}_3)_5\text{SO}_4]\text{Cl}$ and $[\text{Co}(\text{NH}_3)_5\text{Cl}]\text{SO}_4$ are ionisation isomers.
(ii) What is meant by the 'Chelate effect' ? Give an example.
Chemistry.correct:
(a) (i) Diammineargentum(I) dicyanoargentate(I)
(ii) Potassium trioxalatoferrate(III)

OR

(b) (i) Solution of $[\text{Co}(\text{NH}_3)_5\text{SO}_4]\text{Cl}$ gives white precipitate with $\text{AgNO}_3$ ($\text{AgCl}$) but no ppt with $\text{BaCl}_2$. Solution of $[\text{Co}(\text{NH}_3)_5\text{Cl}]\text{SO}_4$ gives white precipitate with $\text{BaCl}_2$ ($\text{BaSO}_4$) but no ppt with $\text{AgNO}_3$.
(ii) Chelate effect: The enhanced stability of complexes formed by chelating (polydentate) ligands compared to unidentate ligands. Example: $[\text{Co}(\text{en})_3]^{3+}$.
Chemistry.solution:
(a) (i) Diammineargentum(I) dicyanoargentate(I)
(ii) Potassium trioxalatoferrate(III)

(b) (i) Ionization test:
$[\text{Co}(\text{NH}_3)_5\text{SO}_4]\text{Cl} + \text{AgNO}_3 \rightarrow \text{AgCl}\downarrow$ (White ppt)
$[\text{Co}(\text{NH}_3)_5\text{Cl}]\text{SO}_4 + \text{BaCl}_2 \rightarrow \text{BaSO}_4}\downarrow$ (White ppt)

(ii) Chelate effect is the thermodynamic stabilization of a coordination compound resulting from the formation of ring structures by polydentate ligands.

Chemistry.text:
Differentiate between the following :
(i) Peptide linkage and Glycosidic linkage
(ii) Essential amino acids and Non-essential amino acids
Chemistry.correct:
(i) Peptide linkage is an amide linkage ($-\text{CO}-\text{NH}-$) formed between $-\text{COOH}$ group of one amino acid and $-\text{NH}_2$ group of another. Glycosidic linkage is an oxide linkage ($-\text{O}-$) formed between two monosaccharide units.
(ii) Essential amino acids cannot be synthesized in the human body and must be supplied through diet (e.g., Valine). Non-essential amino acids can be synthesized in the body (e.g., Glycine).
Chemistry.solution:
(i) Peptide linkage connects amino acids in proteins via amide bond; Glycosidic linkage joins monosaccharides via ether/oxide linkage in carbohydrates.
(ii) Essential amino acids are required from diet; Non-essential amino acids are synthesized internally.

Chemistry.text:
Following reaction takes place in one step :
$2\text{A} + \text{B} \longrightarrow 2\text{C}$
How will the rate of above reaction change if the volume of the reaction vessel is decreased to one third of its original volume ? Will there be any change in the order of reaction with the reduced volume ?
Chemistry.correct:
1. Rate will increase by 27 times.
2. No, there will be no change in the order of reaction.
Chemistry.solution:
Since the reaction takes place in one step, it is an elementary reaction.
Rate law: $R = k [A]^2 [B]^1$
When volume $V$ is reduced to $V/3$, concentrations become 3 times original values ($[A'] = 3[A]$, $[B'] = 3[B]$).
$R' = k (3[A])^2 (3[B]) = 27 k [A]^2 [B] = 27 R$.
The rate increases 27 times. Order of reaction remains $2 + 1 = 3$ (unchanged).

Chemistry.text:
For the first order thermal decomposition reaction, following data was obtained :
$\text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{Cl}(g) \longrightarrow \text{C}_2\text{H}_4(g) + \text{HCl}(g)$

S. No. | Time(s) | Total Pressure (atm)
1 | 0 | 0.30
2 | 30 | 0.50

Calculate rate constant. [Given : $\log 3 = 0.48$]
Chemistry.solution:
At $t = 0$, $P_0 = 0.30\text{ atm}$.
At $t = 30\text{ s}$, reaction: $\text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{Cl} \rightarrow \text{C}_2\text{H}_4 + \text{HCl}$
Initial: $P_0$, 0, 0
At $t$: $P_0 - p$, $p$, $p$
Total pressure $P_t = P_0 + p = 0.30 + p = 0.50\text{ atm} \implies p = 0.20\text{ atm}$.
Pressure of reactant at $t=30\text{ s}$: $P_{\text{reactant}} = P_0 - p = 0.30 - 0.20 = 0.10\text{ atm}$.
$k = \frac{2.303}{t} \log\left(\frac{P_0}{P_0 - p}\right) = \frac{2.303}{30} \log\left(\frac{0.30}{0.10}\right) = \frac{2.303}{30} \log 3 = \frac{2.303 \times 0.48}{30} = 0.036848 \text{ s}^{-1} \approx 3.68 \times 10^{-2} \text{ s}^{-1}$.
Chemistry.topic: Integrated Rate Equations for Gas Phase Reactions

Chemistry.text:
(a) Answer the following :
(i) Why is the Equilibrium Constant ($K_c$) related to $E^\circ_{\text{cell}}$ and not to $E_{\text{cell}}$ ?
(ii) Two metals 'A' and 'B' have standard electrode potential values of $-0.24\text{ V}$ and $+0.80\text{ V}$ respectively. Which of these will liberate hydrogen gas from dil. $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ ?
(iii) Write the cell reaction which occurs in lead storage battery when it is in charging.

OR

(b) What type of battery is Mercury cell ? Why it is more advantageous than dry cell ? Write overall reaction taking place in Mercury cell.
Chemistry.correct:
(a) (i) At equilibrium, $E_{\text{cell}} = 0$, so $E^\circ_{\text{cell}} = \frac{RT}{nF}\ln K_c$.
(ii) Metal 'A' (since its standard reduction potential $-0.24\text{ V}$ is lower/more negative than hydrogen $0.00\text{ V}$).
(iii) $2\text{PbSO}_4(s) + 2\text{H}_2\text{O}(l) \rightarrow \text{Pb}(s) + \text{PbO}_2(s) + 2\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4(aq)$

OR

(b) Primary battery. It provides a constant voltage throughout its life because overall reaction does not involve ions in solution whose concentration changes. Reaction: $\text{Zn(Hg)} + \text{HgO}(s) \rightarrow \text{ZnO}(s) + \text{Hg}(l)$.
Chemistry.solution:
(a) (i) $E_{\text{cell}}$ becomes zero at equilibrium, whereas standard electrode potential $E^\circ_{\text{cell}}$ is constant and related via $\Delta G^\circ = -nFE^\circ_{\text{cell}} = -RT \ln K_c$.
(ii) Metal A has negative standard potential so it acts as a stronger reducing agent than $H_2$ and liberates $H_2$ gas.
(iii) Charging reaction: $2\text{PbSO}_4 + 2\text{H}_2\text{O} \rightarrow \text{Pb} + \text{PbO}_2 + 2\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$.

(b) Mercury cell is a primary cell. Its potential stays constant at ~1.35 V because no ions appear in solution. Overall cell reaction: $\text{Zn(Hg)} + \text{HgO}(s) \rightarrow \text{ZnO}(s) + \text{Hg}(l)$.

Chemistry.text: Calculate the boiling point of a solution containing $0.61\text{ g}$ of benzoic acid (Molar mass = $122\text{ g mol}^{-1}$) in $5\text{ g}$ of $\text{CS}_2$ in which it dimerises to the extent of $88\%$. The boiling point and $K_b$ of $\text{CS}_2$ are $46.2^\circ\text{C}$ and $2.3\text{ K kg mol}^{-1}$ respectively.
Chemistry.solution:
For dimerization $2\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{COOH} \rightleftharpoons (\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{COOH})_2$, degree of association $\alpha = 0.88$, $n = 2$.
$i = 1 - \alpha\left(1 - \frac{1}{n}\right) = 1 - 0.88\left(1 - \frac{1}{2}\right) = 1 - 0.44 = 0.56$.
Molality $m = \frac{w_B / M_B}{w_A \text{ (in kg)}} = \frac{0.61 / 122}{5 / 1000} = \frac{0.005}{0.005} = 1\text{ m}$.
$\Delta T_b = i \cdot K_b \cdot m = 0.56 \times 2.3 \times 1 = 1.288^\circ\text{C}$.
Boiling point of solution $T_b = T_b^0 + \Delta T_b = 46.2 + 1.288 = 47.488^\circ\text{C} \approx 47.49^\circ\text{C}$.
Chemistry.topic: Elevation of Boiling Point and van't Hoff Factor

Chemistry.text:
Write the reactions of D-Glucose with the following :
(a) HI
(b) $\text{Br}_2$ water
(c) Conc. $\text{HNO}_3$
Chemistry.correct:
(a) Prolonged heating with HI yields n-hexane: $\text{C}_6\text{H}_{12}\text{O}_6 \xrightarrow{\text{HI, } \Delta} \text{CH}_3-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}_3$.
(b) Oxidation with $\text{Br}_2$ water gives Gluconic acid: $\text{CHO}-(\text{CHOH})_4-\text{CH}_2\text{OH} \xrightarrow{\text{Br}_2/\text{H}_2\text{O}} \text{COOH}-(\text{CHOH})_4-\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$.
(c) Oxidation with Conc. $\text{HNO}_3$ gives Saccharic acid (Glucaric acid): $\text{CHO}-(\text{CHOH})_4-\text{CH}_2\text{OH} \xrightarrow{\text{HNO}_3} \text{COOH}-(\text{CHOH})_4-\text{COOH}$.
Chemistry.solution:
(a) Glucose heated with HI gives n-hexane.
(b) Mild oxidation with bromine water converts the aldehyde group to carboxylic acid group forming gluconic acid.
(c) Strong oxidation with concentrated nitric acid oxidizes both aldehyde and primary alcohol groups to carboxylic acid forming saccharic acid.

Chemistry.text:
Give reasons for the following :
(a) Carboxylic acids have higher boiling point than alcohols of comparable molecular masses.
(b) Alpha ($\alpha$) hydrogens of aldehydes and ketones are acidic in nature.
(c) Nucleophilic addition of ammonia and its derivatives does not occur with carbonyl group in strongly acidic medium.
Chemistry.correct:
(a) Carboxylic acids form stronger intermolecular hydrogen bonds and exist as stable dimers even in vapor state.
(b) Resonance stabilization of the conjugate base (enolate ion) and strong electron-withdrawing -I effect of the carbonyl group.
(c) In strongly acidic medium, ammonia derivative gets protonated to form an ammonium salt, losing its nucleophilic nature.
Chemistry.solution:
(a) Carboxylic acid molecules form extensive hydrogen-bonded dimers.
(b) The enolate ion formed after loss of $\alpha$-proton is stabilized by resonance.
(c) Strong acid protonates the nucleophile: $\text{NH}_2\text{-Z} + \text{H}^+ \rightarrow \text{NH}_3^+-\text{Z}$, rendering it non-nucleophilic.

Chemistry.text:
Write the reaction involved in the following :
(a) Reimer-Tiemann reaction
(b) Kolbe's reaction
(c) Friedel-Crafts acylation of anisole
Chemistry.correct:
(a) Phenol $+ \text{CHCl}_3 + 3\text{NaOH} \rightarrow \text{Salicylaldehyde (2-hydroxybenzaldehyde)} + 3\text{NaCl} + 2\text{H}_2\text{O}$.
(b) Sodium phenoxide $+ \text{CO}_2 \xrightarrow[2. \text{H}^+]{1. 400\text{ K, 4-7 atm}} \text{Salicylic acid}$.
(c) Anisole $+ \text{CH}_3\text{COCl} \xrightarrow{\text{Anhyd. AlCl}_3} \text{2-Methoxyacetophenone} + \text{4-Methoxyacetophenone}$ (major).
Chemistry.solution:
(a) Reimer-Tiemann reaction converts phenol to salicylaldehyde using chloroform and base.
(b) Kolbe's reaction converts phenoxide to salicylic acid using carbon dioxide.
(c) Friedel-Crafts acylation of anisole yields 2-methoxyacetophenone and 4-methoxyacetophenone.

Chemistry.text:
Compound 'X' with molecular formula $\text{C}_4\text{H}_9\text{Br}$ reacts with aqueous KOH to give an alcohol. The rate of this reaction depends only on the concentration of the compound 'X'. When an optically active isomer 'Y' of the compound 'X' was treated with aqueous KOH solution, the rate of reaction was found to be dependent on concentration of compound 'Y' and aqueous KOH both.
(a) Write down the structural formula of both 'X' and 'Y'.
(b) Out of 'X' and 'Y', which one will undergo racemisation and why ?
(c) Out of 'X' and 'Y', which one will form product with inversion of configuration and why ?
Chemistry.correct:
(a) Compound 'X': 2-Bromo-2-methylpropane / tert-butyl bromide, $(\text{CH}_3)_3\text{C-Br}$.
Compound 'Y': 2-Bromobutane, $\text{CH}_3-\text{CH(Br)}-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}_3$.
(b) 'X' undergoes racemisation via $S_N1$ mechanism because it forms a planar carbocation intermediate.
(c) 'Y' forms product with inversion of configuration via $S_N2$ mechanism because the nucleophile attacks from the backside of the leaving group.
Chemistry.solution:
(a) Reaction of X depends only on [X] $\implies S_N1$ reaction $\implies$ tertiary alkyl halide: $(\text{CH}_3)_3\text{CBr}$ (2-bromo-2-methylpropane). Reaction of Y depends on both [Y] and [KOH] $\implies S_N2$ reaction and Y is optically active $\implies$ chiral secondary alkyl halide: $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(Br)} \text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3$ (2-bromobutane).
(b) X undergoes racemisation via $S_N1$ through planar carbocation.
(c) Y proceeds via $S_N2$ giving Walden inversion.

Chemistry.text:
The reaction of amines with mineral acids to form ammonium salts shows that these are basic in nature. Aliphatic amines are stronger bases than ammonia whereas aromatic amines are weaker bases than ammonia. Aliphatic and aromatic primary and secondary amines react with acid chlorides, anhydrides and esters by nucleophilic substitution reaction. The main problem encountered during electrophilic substitution reactions of aromatic amines is that of their high reactivity. Substitution tends to occur at ortho-and para-positions. Hinsberg reagent is used for the identification and distinction between primary, secondary and tertiary amines. Aryldiazonium salts, usually obtained from arylamines, undergo replacement of the diazonium group with a variety of nucleophiles to provide advantageous methods for producing aryl halides, cyanides, phenols and arenes.

Answer the following questions :
(a) (i) Why $\text{CH}_3 - \text{NH}_2$ is a stronger base than $(\text{CH}_3)_3\text{N}$ in aqueous solution ?
(ii) Write structural formulae of the compound A and B :
$\text{CH}_3\text{CONH}_2 \xrightarrow{\text{NaOBr}} \text{A} \xrightarrow[\text{Base}]{\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{COCl}} \text{B}$
(b) A compound 'X' with molecular formula $\text{C}_3\text{H}_9\text{N}$ reacts with Hinsberg reagent to give a product insoluble in alkali. Identify 'X'.
OR
(b) How can you convert aniline to benzonitrile ?
(c) Why is $-\text{NH}_2$ group of aniline acetylated before carrying out nitration ?
Chemistry.correct:
(a) (i) In aqueous solution, methylamine cation is stabilized by hydrogen bonding/solvation effect to a greater extent than trimethylamine cation due to steric hindrance in the latter.
(ii) Compound A: $\text{CH}_3\text{NH}_2$ (Methylamine)
Compound B: $\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{CONHCH}_3$ (N-Methylbenzamide)
(b) 'X' is a secondary amine: N-methylethanamine / dimethylamine, e.g., $\text{CH}_3-\text{NH}-\text{C}_2\text{H}_5$.
OR
(b) Aniline $\xrightarrow{\text{NaNO}_2 + \text{HCl, 273-278 K}} \text{Benzene diazonium chloride} \xrightarrow{\text{CuCN/KCN}} \text{Benzonitrile}$.
(c) To protect the $-\text{NH}_2$ group and decrease its strong activating effect, thereby preventing multi-substitution and meta-derivative formation.
Chemistry.solution:
(a) (i) Solvation effect and steric hindrance control basic strength in aqueous medium.
(ii) A is formed by Hoffmann bromamide degradation: $\text{CH}_3\text{NH}_2$. Benzoylation gives $\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{CONHCH}_3$.
(b) Secondary amine gives Hinsberg derivative lacking acidic N-H, making it insoluble in alkali.
(c) Acetylation reduces electron density on nitrogen by resonance with acetyl group.

The main problem encountered during electrophilic substitution reactions of aromatic amines is that of their high reactivity. Substitution tends to occur at ortho-and para-positions. Chemistry.text:
The Valence Bond Theory (VBT) explains the formation, magnetic behaviour and geometry of coordination compounds. The Crystal Field Theory (CFT) of coordination compounds is based on the effect of different crystal fields (provided by the ligands taken as point charges), on the degeneracy of d-orbital energies of the central metal atom/ion. The splitting of the d-orbitals provides different electronic arrangements in strong and weak crystal fields.

Answer the following questions :
(a) In octahedral crystal field, energies of which d-orbitals will be raised when ligands approach the central metal atom/ion ? Give reason in support of your answer.
(b) Using crystal field theory, write the electronic configuration of central metal atom/ion of the following :
(i) $[\text{CoF}_6]^{3-}$
(ii) $[\text{Co}(\text{NH}_3)_6]^{3+}$
[At. No. : Co = 27]
(c) $[\text{NiCl}_4]^{2-}$ is paramagnetic while $[\text{Ni}(\text{CO})_4]$ is diamagnetic though both are tetrahedral. Why ? [Atomic No. : Ni = 28]
OR
(c) Write hybridization and magnetic behaviour of the complex $[\text{Fe}(\text{CN})_6]^{3-}$. [Atomic No. : Fe = 26]
Chemistry.correct:
(a) $d_{x^2-y^2}$ and $d_{z^2}$ ($e_g$ orbitals). Reason: These orbitals point directly along the axes where ligands approach, leading to strong electrostatic repulsion.
(b) (i) $[\text{CoF}_6]^{3-}$: $\text{Co}^{3+}$ ($d^6$), weak field: $t_{2g}^4 e_g^2$
(ii) $[\text{Co}(\text{NH}_3)_6]^{3+}$: $\text{Co}^{3+}$ ($d^6$), strong field: $t_{2g}^6 e_g^0$
(c) In $[\text{NiCl}_4]^{2-}$, $\text{Ni}^{2+}$ is $3d^8$ with weak ligand $\text{Cl}^-$, having 2 unpaired electrons ($sp^3$, paramagnetic). In $[\text{Ni(CO)}_4]$, $\text{Ni}^0$ is $3d^8 4s^2$; strong ligand $\text{CO}$ pairs electrons to form $3d^{10}$ ($sp^3$, diamagnetic).
OR
(c) Hybridization: $d^2sp^3$, Magnetic behaviour: Paramagnetic (1 unpaired electron).
Chemistry.solution:
(a) $e_g$ orbitals lie along axes and experience greater repulsion.
(b) CFT configurations for $d^6$ system.
(c) Electronic configuration and pairing by strong field ligand $\text{CO}$ vs weak field $\text{Cl}^-$.
Chemistry.linked_passage: The Valence Bond Theory (VBT) explains the formation, magnetic behaviour and geometry of coordination compounds. The Crystal Field Theory (CFT) of coordination compounds is based on the effect of different crystal fields (provided by the ligands taken as point charges), on the degeneracy of d-orbital energies of the central metal atom/ion. The splitting of the d-orbitals provides different electronic arrangements in strong and weak crystal fields.

Chemistry.text:
(a) (i) From the given data of $E^\circ$ values, answer the following questions :
$E^\circ_{\text{M}^{2+}/\text{M}}$ (V): V (-1.18), Cr (-0.91), Mn (-1.18), Fe (-0.44), Co (-0.28), Ni (-0.25), Cu (+0.34)
(I) Why $E^\circ_{\text{M}^{2+}/\text{M}}$ show irregular trend in the above values ?
(II) Why is $E^\circ_{\text{Cu}^{2+}/\text{Cu}}$ value exceptionally positive ?
(III) Why $E^\circ_{\text{Mn}^{2+}/\text{Mn}}$ value is highly negative ?
(ii) Write the ionic equations for the oxidising action of potassium permanganate for its reaction with $\text{I}^-$ in both acidic and alkaline solutions.

OR

(b) Answer the following questions :
(i) Name a member of the lanthanoid series
(I) which exhibits +4 oxidation state
(II) which exhibits +2 oxidation state.
(ii) Why transition metals act as good catalyst ?
(iii) Why Cr has higher melting point than Mn ?
(iv) What happens when acidic solution of potassium permanganate is allowed to stand for sometime ? Give the equation involved. What is this type of reaction called ?
Chemistry.correct:
(a) (i) (I) Due to irregular variation of ionization enthalpies ($\text{IE}_1 + \text{IE}_2$) and sublimation enthalpies across the 3d series.
(II) High enthalpy of atomization and high ionization enthalpy of Cu are not compensated by its hydration enthalpy.
(III) Due to extra stability of half-filled $d^5$ subshell in $\text{Mn}^{2+}$.
(ii) Acidic: $2\text{MnO}_4^- + 10\text{I}^- + 16\text{H}^+ \rightarrow 2\text{Mn}^{2+} + 5\text{I}_2 + 8\text{H}_2\text{O}$
Alkaline: $2\text{MnO}_4^- + \text{I}^- + \text{H}_2\text{O} \rightarrow 2\text{MnO}_2 + \text{IO}_3^- + 2\text{OH}^-$

OR

(b) (i) (I) Cerium (Ce)
(II) Europium (Eu)
(ii) Due to variable oxidation states and large surface area for adsorption.
(iii) Cr has 6 unpaired electrons per atom ($3d^5 4s^1$) forming strong metallic bonds, whereas Mn has stable $3d^5$ configuration with tightly bound electrons.
(iv) It decomposes slowly releasing oxygen gas: $4\text{MnO}_4^- + 4\text{H}^+ \rightarrow 4\text{MnO}_2 + 3\text{O}_2 + 2\text{H}_2\text{O}$. Autocatalytic reaction.
